title: Adoption Velocity Playbook — 30/60/90 Surge Plan
body:
Purpose:
This is a velocity-focused 30/60/90 onboarding playbook for mid-market customers where fast time-to-value matters and renewal risk is tied to usage within the first 90 days. It combines a standard adoption path with a short 'surge' playbook (intense support/SE hours + tactical experiments) for accounts that show early friction or high upside.

Quick overview (TL;DR):
- Goal: get a production-aimed integration generating measurable inference traffic within 90 days; seed signals for renewal by day 75.
- Primary success metrics: 3 production routes enabled, >=10k tokens/week, SLA smoke tests passing, NPS >= 7 in week 12.
- Surge trigger: <50% of expected weekly token volume by day 21 OR >3 major blockers reported in first 30 days.

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- CSM: cadence, stakeholder alignment, renewal cues, escalations.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration help, runbooks, perf tuning, demo environment.
- Product Manager: prioritize critical bugs, visibility for early regression alerts.
- Customer Eng Contact: technical owner on customer's side.

30-day plan (orientation + unblock):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): onboarding checklist sent, access verified (API keys, IP allowlist), scoring of expected token ramp (CSM/SE estimate).
- Week 1: kickoff (agenda attaches: goals, success metrics, timeline, support model). Quick wins: sample request to hosted API, baseline latency/cost estimate, identify 1 MVP route.
- Week 2: integration pairing session (SE), telemetry plan (logs/metrics/trace tags), run simple eval set (3–5 prompts) for quality baseline.
- Week 3: first internal smoke test; runload small synthetic traffic to validate auth, throttling, error handling. If metrics show <50% of expected traffic, flag for surge.
- Deliverables by day 30: working MVP route, dashboard access for customer, 1-pager with latency/cost baseline, kickoff notes + outstanding risks.

30-day risk triggers (immediate):
- No API connectivity after 5 business days.
- Cost estimation gap > 50% vs expectations.
- >2 production-blocking bugs.

Surge playbook (activate at day 7–21 if trigger fired):
- Blocker triage: 4-hour SLAs for triage, daily standup with SE, CSM, and PM.
- SE deep-dive session: remote pairing for integration, kernel/quantization guidance, and token-batching checklist.
- Short-term config changes: temporary increased burst capacity, change routing policy to fallback model variant, enable prefix/KV caching for hot routes.
- Experimental tactic: deploy trimmed prompt templates to reduce tokens + A/B test on 2 customer segments.
- Communication: 3x weekly status updates, customer-facing timeline with concrete milestones.

60-day plan (stabilize + expand):
- Week 5–6: production hardening (observability hooks, alert thresholds, tracing), run a 24–48h continuous throughput test at target QPS.
- Week 7: adoption workshop: map out 3 product use cases, identify owners, document success criteria.
- Week 8: cost/perf optimization session from Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quant profiles).
- Deliverables by day 60: expanded routes (2–3), optimized config suggestions implemented, initial usage trend report for CSM.

90-day plan (scale + renewal prep):
- Week 9–10: measure outcomes vs success metrics; produce a one-page renewal health snapshot (usage, SLOs met, risks, roadmap asks).
- Week 11: executive alignment call (CSM + customer execs + renewal owner).
- Week 12: renewal/expansion proposal drafted if targets met; otherwise outline remediation plan + new KPIs.
- Deliverables by day 90: renewal health snapshot, proposed next-phase capacity plan, playbook notes captured.

Renewal cues & play actions:
- Green: usage >= 85% of forecast + SLOs met -> standard renewal outreach + expansion conversation.
- Yellow: 50–85% usage OR 1 SLO missed -> propose 30-day remediation + targeted SE hours.
- Red: <50% usage OR >2 major incidents -> schedule exit interview, propose pilot pause or migration support.

Lightweight evaluation & QBR artifacts (what CSM ships at 90 days):
- 1-page health snapshot (metrics: tokens/week, p50/p95 latency, errors, cost delta).
- 3 annotated prompts used for quality monitoring + example model outputs.
- Runbook excerpts: how to reproduce common issues, who to call (on-call links).
- Proposed next steps & recommended SLA/commit (redwood/dedicated/private suggestions).

Email templates (snippets):
- Kickoff invite: short agenda + ask to share 3 top success metrics; include confluence and runbook links.
- Surge update: subject line "Surge status: {account} — next 48h" with bullets "today, blockers, next actions, owner".
- Renewal touch: subject "90-day health for {account} — renewal check" with quick bullets and link to one-page health snapshot.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- How aggressive should default token forecasts be for new customers vs based on product tier?
- Need template for expected SE hours per tier + pricing approvals for surge overages.
- Consider adding a short postmortem template for accounts that churn within 180 days.

Quick checklist (copyable):
- [ ] API keys provisioned and validated
- [ ] Dashboard access granted to customer admins
- [ ] MVP route accepting 1k qps smoke test
- [ ] 3 prompts baseline quality eval
- [ ] Runbook with contact points created
- [ ] Renewal snapshot drafted by day 75

Appendix: sample KPI targets (example only)
- Early-adopter SMB: target 2k tokens/week by day 30, 8k by day 90, NPS target 6+
- Mid-market product team: target 10k tokens/week by day 60, production SLO p95 < 600ms, NPS 7+

References / links to internal artifacts:
- Onboarding snippet repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-snippets
- SE tuning checklist (draft): https://confluence.company/SE-tuning-checklist
- Renewal playbook draft: https://confluence.company/Renewals-Playbook-draft

Revision history (notes):
- 2024-09-18 initial draft by Jordan Kim
- 2024-09-24 added surge playbook and checklist after SE sync
- 2024-10-02 updated metrics and added sample KPI table (in review)
